title: Loss of anonymity ends an AC's career whether or not they were at fault
content:
A.1.5.7 states that the Facilitator and Aligned Delegate roles "require anonymity and high levels of operational security," that breaches "are considered serious misalignment," and then specifies the consequence: "the known identities of individuals holding these AC roles shall be promptly derecognized, and they will be barred from further participation as Alignment Conservers."

The operative phrase is "the known identities." The trigger is the *state of being known*, not an act of carelessness. Someone doxxed by a determined third party, or exposed through a counterparty's failure, is in the same position as someone who published their own name — derecognized, and permanently excluded from the AC track.

This is not a punishment provision even though it sits among misalignment rules; it is a containment provision. A pseudonymous delegate's protection against bribery, coercion, and retaliation is entirely a function of not being identifiable. Once identity is public, that protection is gone and cannot be restored, so continued service would leave a known, pressurable actor holding delegated voting power. The bar on further participation follows for the same reason: anonymity is not re-establishable.

The Action Tenet at A.1.5.7.0.4.1 shows how demanding the maintenance obligation is — practices "must go beyond basic privacy-enhancing measures" and include "secure communication channels, stringent data encryption, anonymity tools like VPNs and TOR networks, regular security audits, and rigorous digital footprint management."

The cost is a role with an irreversible, partly exogenous career risk, which narrows the candidate pool to people able to sustain sophisticated opsec indefinitely. That is a real constraint on who can hold governance power in Sky, and it is chosen deliberately over the alternative of accountable public delegates.
description: A.1.5.7 requires that known identities of AD and Facilitator role holders be promptly derecognized and barred from further AC participation — an outcome driven by exposure, not culpability.
